The incident gamma ray rate is given by the total gamma emission rate (2 gammas per decay) times the fraction of solid angle subtended by the patient:  
\[
\text{Rate} = 2 \times (3.0 \times 10^{14}) \times \frac{0.30}{4\pi (4.0)^2} = \frac{1.8 \times 10^{14}}{64\pi} \approx 8.95 \times 10^{11} \text{ Bq}.
\]  
Thus \(X = 8.95\).

For antiproton production, the reaction is \(p + p \rightarrow p + p + p + \bar{p}\). The minimum lab kinetic energy of the incident proton is  
\[
K_{\text{min}} = 6 m_p c^2 = 6 \times 938.272 \text{ MeV} \approx 5629.6 \text{ MeV} \approx 5630 \text{ MeV}.
\]  
Thus the required kinetic energy is about 5630 MeV.

ANSWER: 8.95,5630
